title: The null factor law
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches similar shapes and scale factor, not the null factor law for solving products equal to zero, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: The null factor law
card: If two numbers multiply to give zero, at least one of them must be zero. This is the null factor law.
Solve each factor separately. Here \(x - 2 = 0\) gives \(x = 2\), and \(x + 5 = 0\) gives \(x = -5\).
The law only works when the product equals zero. If the product equals another number, such as \((x - 2)(x + 5) = 8\), you cannot set each factor equal to 8.
draft.remember: When a product is zero, set each factor to zero and solve each one.

a.why: Set each factor to zero. \(x - 3 = 0\) gives \(x = 3\), and \(x + 4 = 0\) gives \(x = -4\). The option with \(x = -3\) or \(x = 4\) has the signs swapped.
a.clue: Which value of \(x\) makes each bracket equal zero?

b.q: Mia says \(x(x - 6) = 0\) has only one solution, \(x = 6\). Which statement is correct?
opts: It has one solution, \(x = 6\), as Mia says
It has one solution, \(x = 0\), from the first factor
b.why: The factors are \(x\) and \(x - 6\). Setting each to zero gives \(x = 0\) or \(x = 6\). Mia left out the first factor, but \(x\) can be zero too. Check: \(0 \times (0 - 6) = 0\).
b.clue: The lone \(x\) is a factor as well.
